walkthroughs.body_html:
Using the Environment — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Using the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Using the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An organism's role in an ecosystem is its?
options: Habitat
Niche
Population
Biome

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Stopping all development immediately.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
Environmental protection at all costs.

mcqs.q: Why are invasive species often more harmful than native species?
options: They lack natural predators or competitors in their new environment, so they spread unchecked.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
They are larger than native species.
They are inherently more aggressive than native species.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Habitat”?
options: Living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria.
Group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
Specific place where an organism lives, providing its required abiotic and biotic conditions.
Community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Niche”?
options: Community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.
Role an organism plays in its ecosystem - what it eats, how it interacts, when it is active.
Non-living components: light, temperature, water, soil pH, oxygen.
Living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Abiotic factors”?
options: Specific place where an organism lives, providing its required abiotic and biotic conditions.
Living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria.
Group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
Non-living components: light, temperature, water, soil pH, oxygen.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Population”?
options: Group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
Role an organism plays in its ecosystem - what it eats, how it interacts, when it is active.
Community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.
Non-living components: light, temperature, water, soil pH, oxygen.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ecosystem”?
options: Community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.
Non-living components: light, temperature, water, soil pH, oxygen.
Role an organism plays in its ecosystem - what it eats, how it interacts, when it is active.
Living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Biotic factors”?
options: Non-living components: light, temperature, water, soil pH, oxygen.
Living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria.
Community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.
Group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
